entries.rationale: A function may define a meaningful boundary even when it currently has one caller.
entries.safety_invariant: Function and file-size rails still reject unbounded indirection and growth.
entries.alternatives_considered: Inlining every single-call function couples concerns and makes large files harder to decompose.
entries.substitute: structural component limits and maintainability review

entries.rationale: Short lifetime names are the established Rust convention in compact generic signatures.
entries.safety_invariant: Complex lifetime relationships still require readable type structure and compiler validation.
entries.alternatives_considered: Verbose names do not improve simple two-lifetime relationships.
entries.substitute: compiler borrow checking and signature review
entries.re_review_phase: Only if project naming policy changes

entries.rationale: LocalHold targets the standard library and has no no_std allocation contract.
entries.safety_invariant: The supported platform contract explicitly includes std.
entries.alternatives_considered: Using alloc paths would imply portability the project does not test or support.
entries.substitute: documented platform and Rust-version support policy
entries.evidence: Runtime, filesystem, networking, and database dependencies require std
entries.re_review_phase: Only if no_std becomes a supported target

entries.rationale: LocalHold is a std application and consistently imports language and runtime facilities through std.
entries.safety_invariant: The supported platform contract explicitly includes std.
entries.alternatives_considered: Mixing core and std imports provides no supported portability benefit.
entries.substitute: documented platform and Rust-version support policy
entries.re_review_phase: Only if no_std becomes a supported target

entries.rationale: Rust integration tests are separate targets by design and inline tests may sit beside the behavior they verify.
entries.safety_invariant: The structural classifier independently identifies every test target and test-only cfg branch.
entries.alternatives_considered: Forcing one module shape would not improve test isolation or signal.
entries.substitute: cfg-aware source classification and explicit test-target inventory

entries.rationale: The current crate has not yet separated proven-bound indexing from unchecked indexing at a practical lint level.
entries.safety_invariant: Production panic paths remain governed by panic and unwrap policies and explicit expectations are inventoried when this lint is locally raised.
entries.alternatives_considered: Immediately warning globally would create a large unaudited migration that obscures higher-priority unsafe and structural recovery.
entries.substitute: bounds reasoning, panic-path tests, and exact local expectations
entries.evidence: Current global lint configuration and source inventory

entries.rationale: The root test policy still permits unwrap while shipped production profiles override this setting to deny.
entries.safety_invariant: Every shipped library and binary profile denies unwrap_used; this allowance is only the temporary default for tests.
entries.alternatives_considered: A global deny before the test audit would create low-signal churn and encourage blanket local expectations.
entries.substitute: closed production Clippy matrix with command-line deny and sentinels
entries.evidence: Production profile matrix and test-only unwrap sentinel
